Data:Collaborate.xere.json.label: Collaborate: Ereb
Data:Collaborate.xere.json.startdescription: My pride will find an echo in theirs. [Boosts Grail and Edge]

Data:Collaborate.xfet.json.label: Collaborate: Fet
Data:Collaborate.xfet.json.startdescription: Perhaps we shared a dream. [Boosts Rose and Moth]
Data:Collaborate.xfet.json.desc: My assistant and I have an unspoken understanding.

Data:Collaborate.xhea.json.label: Collaborate: Health
Data:Collaborate.xhea.json.startdescription: I'm ready to lend my limbs. [Boosts Heart, Scale, Nectar]

Data:Collaborate.xmet.json.label: Collaborate: Mettle
Data:Collaborate.xmet.json.startdescription: Inspiration and determination. [Boosts Forge and Edge]

Data:Collaborate.xpho.json.label: Collaborate: Phost
Data:Collaborate.xpho.json.startdescription: Together, we'll be watchful. [Boosts Lantern and Sky]
Data:Collaborate.xpho.json.desc: My assistant and I are vigilant.

Data:Collaborate.xsha.json.label: Collaborate: Shapt
Data:Collaborate.xsha.json.startdescription: Education, or beguilement? [Boosts Knock and Forge]
Data:Collaborate.xsha.json.desc: My assistant and I fall easily into conversation.

Data:Collaborate.xtri.json.label: Collaborate: Trist
Data:Collaborate.xtri.json.startdescription: Secret sorrows may join our strengths. [Boosts Moth and Moon]
Data:Collaborate.xtri.json.desc: What comes? Neither of us knows yet, but we will.

Data:Collaborate.xwis.json.label: Collaborate: Wist
Data:Collaborate.xwis.json.startdescription: We'll watch for what lies ahead. [Boosts Winter and Lantern]
Data:Collaborate.xwis.json.desc: My assistant and I will be prudent.

Data:Collection.busts.json.label: Librarians Past, Present, Future
Data:Collection.busts.json.startdescription: I am the twelfth Librarian of Hush House...
Data:Collection.busts.json.desc: I am the twelfth Librarian of Hush House; and I, too, will be remembered.

Data:Comfort.json.label: Comfort
Data:Comfort.json.desc: Hush House has been called 'bleak', but usually only by those who have never been inside.

Data:Commit.bir.s.hill.hollow.json.label: How They Began
Data:Commit.bir.s.hill.hollow.json.startdescription: In the beginning, the Carapace Cross served the first Hours, the gods born from stone. And the first of the Carapace Cross were the Thritige-kind, who sought the Monarch-at-the-Crossroads to rule them wisely and found him in themselves, who began as many and ended as one. This is a riddle, and the riddlemakers know its importance.
Data:Commit.bir.s.hill.hollow.json.desc: In the beginning, the Carapace Cross served the first Hours, the gods born from stone. And the first of the Carapace Cross were the Thritige-kind, who sought the Monarch-at-the-Crossroads to rule them wisely and found him in themselves, who began as many and ended as one.

Data:Commit.bir.s.leaves.thorns.json.label: Looking Up
Data:Commit.bir.s.leaves.thorns.json.startdescription: The gardener's first lesson is this: look up. What starts as weather ends in the world, what starts as sky ends in the soil. This is what the birds know, and the birds know most things first.
Data:Commit.bir.s.leaves.thorns.json.desc: The gardener's first lesson is this: look up. What starts as weather ends in the world, what starts as sky ends in the soil. This is what the birds know, and the birds know most things first.

Data:Commit.bir.s.path.pilgrim.json.label: The Threshold
Data:Commit.bir.s.path.pilgrim.json.startdescription: Every traveller crosses a threshold twice. The Horned-Axe is the Hour who faces both ways at every threshold. Find the answer to her riddles in Birdsong.
Data:Commit.bir.s.path.pilgrim.json.desc: Every traveller crosses a threshold twice. The Horned-Axe is the Hour who faces both ways at every threshold.

Data:Commit.bir.s.pentiments.precursors..label: Coral
Data:Commit.bir.s.pentiments.precursors..startdescription: Of the Ligeian Medusa, it has been said: 'She might be the oldest of her kind still living; and she is dead.' Symurgists might interpret this thus: she is the oldest of the shared Names of the Twins - the Hours we call Sister-and-Witch, Witch-and-Sister.

Data:Commit.bir.s.ramsund.json.label: The Falconer's Tale
Data:Commit.bir.s.ramsund.json.startdescription: There's a very old story told by falconers about the aviform Hours - the secret gods who take the shape of birds. Once there were only five - the dove, the crow, the laughingthrush, the twin kites. The sixth had fallen to the talons of an owl, and they sought another to join their company. But the crow rejected half of all those they found,  for the dowdiness of their plumage, and the dove rejected the others, for being too gaudy. At last they found a night-bird whose feathers were both the perfect white and the perfect black of the crow and of the dove. But once they had accepted him they learnt he was no bird at all - only a night-flitting moth. Fortunately for the moth, their pride kept them from admitting their mistake; but since that day, the aviform Hours will only meet at night, when the sixth of their kind won't be unmasked.

Data:Commit.bir.s.rhyme.remembrance.json.label: What We Were?
Data:Commit.bir.s.rhyme.remembrance.json.startdescription:
The shapes that loped beside you in the frost,
The scraps you gleaned of caul and periost
Once these were answers to 'What May Be Lost?'.

All part of the matter we call Birdsong.
Data:Commit.bir.s.rhyme.remembrance.json.desc:
The shapes that loped beside you in the frost,
The scraps you gleaned of caul and periost
Once these were answers to 'What May Be Lost?'

Data:Commit.bir.s.sabazine.json.label: The Fisher's Tale
Data:Commit.bir.s.sabazine.json.startdescription: There's a story told by fisherfolk, about a city of amber and orichalcum that lies behind the waves. Those who eat of its fruits can breathe water and drink light, but they can never drink anything else afterwards. Only in another History, they say; but if you tie your nets right, you might just catch one of its citizens in this History, and they might just tell you the way.
Data:Commit.bir.s.sabazine.json.desc: There's a story told beside the sea, of a city of amber and orichalcum that lies behind the waves. Those who eat of its fruits can breathe water and drink light, but they can never drink anything else afterwards. Only in another History, they say; but if you tie your nets right, you might just catch one of its citizens in this History, and they might just tell you the way.

Data:Commit.bir.s.sandstories.json.label: A City
Data:Commit.bir.s.sandstories.json.startdescription: The seven tainted immortals we call Ligeians are relentless in their appetite, and outcast under the laws of heaven. But they have their uses to the Hours. The Ligeian Kleidouchos has known all the great keys, and even now she holds the Key of Days; so every year she meets the Vagabond in Vienna, to exchange the names of lesser keys for the stories of the Vagabond's travels. We call their gossip Birdsong.

Data:Commit.bir.s.seastories.json.label: The Sea-Born
Data:Commit.bir.s.seastories.json.startdescription: The Ligeian Morgen, holder of the key of black sapphire, called sea-born, tide-drawn. Did she come from Ys behind the wave? If we speak her name at the rising of the moon, can we summon that old song of flutes and bells? These are Birdsong-riddles.
Data:Commit.bir.s.seastories.json.desc: The Ligeian Morgen, holder of the key of black sapphire, called sea-born, tide-drawn. Did she come from Ys behind the wave? If we speak her name at the rising of the moon, can we summon that old song of flutes and bells?

Data:Commit.bir.s.skystories.json.label: The Roost
Data:Commit.bir.s.skystories.json.startdescription:
A thief of sights, a scavenger of thrones,
A border-reaver and a thief of knots
A thief of colours and a thief of bones.

This is Birdsong.
Data:Commit.bir.s.skystories.json.desc:
A thief of sights, a scavenger of thrones,
A border-reaver and a thief of knots
A thief of colours and a thief of bones.

Data:Commit.bir.s.snowstories.json.label: Much Remains
Data:Commit.bir.s.snowstories.json.startdescription:
Medusa's Riddle, first: What Is Not Seen?
The Night, the Heart, the Moon, the Day. Between.
The palest key. The birth-scarred Coil Queen.

This is Birdsong.
Data:Commit.bir.s.snowstories.json.desc:
Medusa's Riddle, first: What Is Not Seen?
The Night, the Heart, the Moon, the Day. Between.
The palest key. The birth-scarred Coil Queen.

Data:Commit.bir.s.stonestories.json.label: A Vengeance
Data:Commit.bir.s.stonestories.json.startdescription: The Hours once called Flint and the Wheel are gone, but the blood of their Name-emanations was mingled with the blood of mortals, and from it sprang the line of Antaios. Be careful: if enough Antaian blood is spilled, the Flint and the Wheel might wake. This is remembered in the songs of warning.
Data:Commit.bir.s.stonestories.json.desc: The Hours once called Flint and the Wheel are gone, but the blood of their Name-emanations was mingled with the blood of mortals, and from it sprang the line of Antaios. Be careful: if enough Antaian blood is spilled, the Flint and the Wheel might wake.

Data:Commit.bir.s.strings.songs.json.label: The Round
Data:Commit.bir.s.strings.songs.json.startdescription: There are no words in the song of birds; so birdsong had no beginning and will have no end.
Data:Commit.bir.s.strings.songs.json.desc: There are no words in the song of birds; so birdsong had no beginning and will have no end.

Data:Commit.bir.s.vak.json.label: An Opportunity
Data:Commit.bir.s.vak.json.startdescription: Something not commonly understood: were there no Calyptra to conceal perilous knowledge, there could be no Vak. A door opens both ways. This is understood by scholars of the Arts Unregarded.
Data:Commit.bir.s.vak.json.desc: Something not commonly understood: were there no Calyptra to conceal perilous knowledge, there could be no Vak. A door opens both ways.

Data:Commit.bir.s.weaving.knotworking.js.label: What Remains
Data:Commit.bir.s.weaving.knotworking.js.startdescription: Cut a thread, and the tapestry remains. Birdsong follows the thread.
Data:Commit.bir.s.weaving.knotworking.js.desc: Cut a thread, and the tapestry remains.

Data:Commit.bir.s.wolfstories.json.label: The Wolf's Return
Data:Commit.bir.s.wolfstories.json.startdescription: The Sanctioned Version of the Book of Suns says that the Wolf-Divided was awoken by the Sun's division. We know from this that the Wolf was its own Hour even when the Sun was whole. So we glean and we guess that the Sun might be healed, and the Wolf return to its slumbers. So we glean and guess that a Second Dawn would bring peace, but the Wolf will fight to prevent it. This is Birdsong.

So we glean and guess that a Second Dawn would bring peace, but the Wolf will fight to prevent it.

Data:Commit.bos.s.applebrighteuphonies.j.label: What May Be Known
Data:Commit.bos.s.applebrighteuphonies.j.startdescription: Calyptra is the law that requires secret knowledge to be concealed - except in the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. The number of the Hours of the Calyptra is three, and we do not speak of the oldest Hour. This observance is a matter of Bosk.
Data:Commit.bos.s.applebrighteuphonies.j.desc: Calyptra is the law that requires secret knowledge to be concealed - except in the libraries of the Watchman's Tree. The number of the Hours of the Calyptra is three, and we do not speak of the oldest Hour, though we remember her.

Data:Commit.bos.s.desires.dissolutions.j.label: Underneath
Data:Commit.bos.s.desires.dissolutions.j.startdescription:
RED THE DAWN AND BLACK THE NIGHT AND WHITE WHAT'S LEFT. ABOVE WE SEE, BENEATH WE KNOW.

Bosk.
Data:Commit.bos.s.desires.dissolutions.j.desc: RED THE DAWN AND BLACK THE NIGHT AND WHITE WHAT'S LEFT. ABOVE WE SEE, BENEATH WE KNOW.

Data:Commit.bos.s.drums.dances.json.label: The Root
Data:Commit.bos.s.drums.dances.json.startdescription: The Thunderskin, the eternal drum that beats to preserve the skin of the world, is a god-from-flesh, which is to say he was once mortal. He died to preserve the last god-from-stone; he died for love; he died for necessity. In matters of Bosk, these three are often intertwined.

Data:Commit.bos.s.furs.feathers.json.label: The Well in the Wood
Data:Commit.bos.s.furs.feathers.json.startdescription: When the first hunters were starving in the Wood, in the days before its darkening, they found a deep and crimson well. In it they drowned the beasts of the earth, so that the beasts would be reborn threefold, and the hunters could feast. So the Red Grail came to be, and so ever since she feeds us and she feeds upon us. This, the Matriarchs of the Knot have taught us.

Data:Commit.bos.s.henavek.json.label: The Roots
Data:Commit.bos.s.henavek.json.startdescription: A farmers' proverb in Brancrug: 'What starts in the roots, ends in the sky.'  A superstition goes with it, that before a child's first birthday you should leave her for a summer night sleeping in the roots of an apple-tree, to make sure she grows tall and straight-backed. Not many pay heed to the superstition now, but everyone remembers the proverb. It would probably count as Bosk.

Data:Commit.bos.s.herbs.infusions.json.label: The Root and the Source
Data:Commit.bos.s.herbs.infusions.json.startdescription: In the inmost walled garden of the palace of the Shadowless Kings in Persia, there grew a yew-tree older than any other. Its root was red, its flowers were black, its berries were white. The Kings would leave their girl-children overnight in the nest of its roots, in memory of the great Mother of their line, and so their daughters were assured health, longevity and wisdom. This is the source of all our science, and this is Bosk.

Data:Commit.bos.s.horns.ivories.json.label: The Moth's Way
Data:Commit.bos.s.horns.ivories.json.startdescription: When the Moth goes a-hunting in the dark of the Wood, he remembers a time when the Wood was bright, but he uses his horns to find the way, and we may follow him if we choose. After all, a trophy is nothing without a hunt: that's the lesson of the Wood.

Data:Commit.bos.s.insects.nectars.json.label: The Grail's Favourlings
Data:Commit.bos.s.insects.nectars.json.startdescription: The bright-winged, dark-winged Glaeterfleoge-kind called themselves the Grail's favourlings. They are gone now, like all the Carapace-kinds, but we can still use the arts of the Hive to glean the sweetness in the hidden places of the Wood; the legacy of the Carapace Cross; Bosk.
Data:Commit.bos.s.insects.nectars.json.desc: The bright-winged, dark-winged Glaeterfleoge-kind called themselves the Grail's favourlings. Data:Commit.bos.s.killasimi.json.label: The Weaver's Tale
Data:Commit.bos.s.killasimi.json.startdescription: There is a prophecy among weavers: of one who will unwisely seek to find the future in a tapestry of her own hair. Her house will grow dark, shrouded in the labyrinths of her tresses. Pilgrims will seek her in the cellar of her house, where she will plead with them to cut her free. They will always fail, and she will always devour them. At last one will come who will ask instead to stay with her. Others will join them, until the house becomes a palace and the palace a city, below the world, where all are welcome and in the tapestry all truths are revealed.
Data:Commit.bos.s.killasimi.json.desc: There is a prophecy of a master-weaver who will unwisely seek to find the future in a tapestry of her own hair. Her house will grow dark, shrouded in the labyrinths of her tresses. Pilgrims will seek her in the cellar of her house, where she will plead with them to cut her free. They will always fail, and she will always devour them. At last one will come who will ask instead to stay with her. Others will join them, until the house becomes a palace and the palace a city, below the world, where all are welcome and in the tapestry all truths are revealed.

Data:Commit.bos.s.leaves.thorns.json.label: Looking Down
Data:Commit.bos.s.leaves.thorns.json.startdescription: The gardener's first lesson is this: know your thorns, know your poisons. There's no point thinking about tomorrow when we aren't expecting to live through today. This is the lesson our ancestors learnt the hard way in the Wood: this is Bosk.
Data:Commit.bos.s.leaves.thorns.json.desc: The gardener's first lesson is this: know your thorns, know your poisons. There's no point thinking about tomorrow when we aren't expecting to live through today. This is the lesson our ancestors learnt the hard way in the Wood: this is Bosk.

Data:Commit.bos.s.orchids.narcotics.json.label: The Grail's Births
Data:Commit.bos.s.orchids.narcotics.json.startdescription: Learn from blood and drink from the earth. The Red Grail brought forth the Hours called Flowermaker and Beachcrow, who know where in the wood we can find delight. These are the temptations of Bosk.
Data:Commit.bos.s.orchids.narcotics.json.desc: Learn from blood and drink from the earth. The Red Grail brought forth the Hours called Flowermaker and Beachcrow, who know where in the wood we can find delight.

Data:Commit.bos.s.pearl.tide.json.label: What Returns
Data:Commit.bos.s.pearl.tide.json.startdescription: The Sea accepts every gift it is given, and sometimes, now and then, those gifts are returned. The Red Grail slew the Hour named Tide, and what remained was given to the Sea; so, perhaps, one day, that Hour might return. This is life, and so this is Bosk.
Data:Commit.bos.s.pearl.tide.json.desc: The Sea accepts every gift it is given, and sometimes, now and then, those gifts are returned. The Red Grail slew the Hour named Tide, and what remained was given to the Sea; so, perhaps, one day, that Hour might return.

Data:Commit.bos.s.resurgences.emergences.label: Grail and Moth
Data:Commit.bos.s.resurgences.emergences.startdescription: The gods-from-Stone made a law that the keys of dream cannot be held or owned. The time of Stone is past, but the keys remain. So the holders of these keys can only be the seven Ligeians, whose crime has set them outside the law. But the Ligeians serve an Hour of Grail and Moth: when the last remnants of the gods-from-Stone are consumed, the law will be consumed with them. Bosk is the wisdom of change.
